newsitem.title: JAPAN: Top LDP official says party needs coalition ally.
newsitem.headline: Top LDP official says party needs coalition ally.

text.p: Japan's Liberal Democratic Party will be unable to form a government on its own after Sunday's general election and needs coalition partners, a senior LDP official said.

"In order to secure a comfortable majority of 270 seats in parliament we will have to form a coalition," Taku Yamasaki, head of the LDP's policy research council, told a news conference at party headquarters.

Parliament members and pundits have been saying the LDP may try to continue its current coalition with the Social Democrats even if it wins a majority in Sunday's general elections for the Lower House, because it lacks a majority in the Upper House.
The powerful Lower House holds constitutional precedence over the Upper House in the naming of the prime minister, passing state budgets and ratifying treaties.

But an Upper House hostile to the government can considerably delay or even kill non-budget bills. The LDP holds only 108 seats in the 252-seat Upper House, which cannot be dissolved but instead has elections for half its members every three years. The next Upper House election is in 1998. The Social Democrats hold 36 seats in the Upper House.
